exec_summary: Site traffic (GA4, 2026-05-02 to 2026-05-08): growthbook.io had 12,709 sessions and 7,950 users (+9.2% week over week).

GrowthBook's organic search clicks dipped 9% week-over-week (3,432 vs. 3,776 — GSC, organic only), but the decline is almost entirely explained by the homepage losing 172 branded clicks, not a broad organic slide. The rest of the site held steady or grew. GA4 all-traffic sessions tell a healthier story: 12,709 sessions this week, up 9.2% WoW, with Direct (6,312) and Organic Search (5,116) as the top channels. Impressions actually jumped from 144K to 167K, signaling growing visibility. Notably, GrowthBook published five new blog posts this week — 'What Is A/B Testing' (28 clicks, 57K impressions, position 7.8), 'What Are Feature Flags' (20 clicks, 31K impressions), 'A/B Testing in the Age of AI' (22 clicks), '7 Steps to Better Experiment Design' (15 clicks), and 'Holdouts in GrowthBook' (11 clicks) — strong early traction for fresh content. Comparison pages are soft: 15 total clicks this week vs. 18 last, with the vs-PostHog page declining most sharply (2 vs. 1 clicks 7d, but 4 vs. 14 over 28d).

The single most important strategic finding this week is Optimizely's coordinated launch of at least 10 vertical- and page-type-specific experimentation use case posts across retail, financial services, and healthcare. This is a deliberate bottom-of-funnel SEO play targeting buyers in regulated and high-value industries who are searching for proof that experimentation works in their specific context. GrowthBook has no equivalent vertical use case content, which means Optimizely is building a moat around high-intent, industry-specific queries before GrowthBook even enters those conversations.

Optimizely dominated competitor activity this week with a batch publish of use-case content spanning retail (homepage, checkout, category, product, search results, subscription) and financial services and healthcare pages — all scored as Tier 1 relevance threats. PostHog published 143 new pages (primarily docs and integration content, threat 5) and Harness published 29 new blog posts (threat 5–6). LaunchDarkly, Statsig, Eppo, Unleash, and Flagsmith showed sitemap fetch failures or large URL count drops this week — their new content could not be verified and will be rechecked next run.
content_recommendations: 1. Write a 'GrowthBook for Financial Services' experimentation use case page targeting queries like 'A/B testing for banks' and 'experimentation in fintech' — Optimizely just published three financial services-specific use case posts (homepage, mobile, offer page) and GrowthBook has zero content in this vertical, creating an immediate gap before Optimizely earns rankings.

2. Write a 'GrowthBook for Retail' experimentation use case hub (or series) covering checkout, homepage, and product page testing — Optimizely published five retail-specific posts this week, and retail is a high-intent vertical where buyers evaluate platforms based on industry fit, not just features.

3. Optimize the 'experimentation platform' and 'a/b testing platform' pages or posts to push from position 13 and 10 respectively into the top 5 — both queries have 400+ impressions this week and are classic high-intent, high-value terms where a position improvement from 13 to 7 would likely triple clicks.

4. Expand the 'What Is A/B Testing' blog post (currently 28 clicks, position 7.8, 57K impressions) with deeper structured content, FAQs, and schema markup — it is the highest-impression new post by a wide margin and is one good optimization cycle away from a top-5 ranking that could drive hundreds of clicks weekly.

5. Refresh the GrowthBook vs. PostHog comparison page — it dropped from 14 clicks (28d prior) to 4 clicks (28d current), the steepest 28-day decline in the comparison portfolio, and with PostHog being a direct open-source competitor, this page needs updated positioning and stronger targeting of 'posthog alternative' queries to recover.
